1.name: Crankcase, right half
1.spec: Split on the crank's vertical plane
1.note: One of two castings bolted together on the crank's centre line. It carries the main bearings, the camshaft, and cylinders 1 and 3 on its pads.

2.name: Crankcase, left half
2.spec: Split on the crank's vertical plane
2.note: The mirror casting for cylinders 2 and 4. Its pads sit 55 mm aft of the right half's, so each pair of opposed rods can share the crank.

3.name: Main bearing shell
3.note: Thin oil-fed shells the crank's journals run on. The front pair also takes the propeller's pull or push along the shaft.

4.name: Crankshaft, four throws, propeller flange
4.note: Turns the pistons' push into rotation. The propeller bolts straight to its nose flange: no gearbox, so the propeller turns at engine speed.

5.name: Connecting rod
5.note: Links each piston to its crankpin. Opposed rods sit on throws 180° apart, so the two pistons of a pair move out and in together.

6.name: Piston
6.note: Takes the burning charge's pressure on its crown. Each opposed pair moves in mirror image, so their shaking forces cancel.

7.name: Piston ring set
7.note: Two compression rings seal the gas above the piston; the oil ring wipes the bore so oil stays out of the chamber.

8.name: Piston pin
8.note: Joins rod and piston. Soft aluminium plugs in its ends stop a floating pin from scoring the barrel wall.

9.name: Cylinder barrel, finned
9.note: A steel sleeve with deep fins: the air rammed through the cowling carries the heat away. There is no water jacket.

10.name: Cylinder head with rocker box
10.spec: Screwed and shrunk on the barrel
10.note: Forms the domed chamber, holds both valves and both plugs, and houses the rockers in a box cast into its top.

11.name: Valve, inlet / exhaust
11.note: Opens to let the charge in or the burned gas out. The exhaust valve runs red hot, so it is made of a nickel superalloy.

12.name: Valve spring pair and retainer
12.note: Two nested springs close the valve. If one breaks the other still holds the valve off the piston: a redundancy aircraft engines need.

13.name: Rocker arm
13.note: A lever on a shaft in the rocker box: the pushrod lifts one end, the other end pushes the valve open 1.45 times as far.

14.name: Pushrod and shroud tube
14.note: Carries the tappet's lift out to the rocker. It is hollow: oil from the tappet flows up it to oil the rockers.

15.name: Hydraulic tappet
15.note: Rides on the cam. Oil trapped under its plunger by a check ball takes up all clearance, so the valves need no lash setting.

16.name: Camshaft
16.spec: Above the crankshaft, half crank speed
16.note: Gear-driven at half crank speed. Its lobes set when each valve opens and closes, so each opens once every two turns.

17.name: Spark plug
17.note: Each cylinder has a top and a bottom plug, fed by different magnetos. Two flames burn the charge faster, and one can fail safely.

18.name: Rocker box cover
18.note: Closes the rocker box and keeps in the oil that comes up the pushrods.

19.name: Crankshaft gear
19.note: On the crank's rear end: it drives the accessories, the magnetos at crank speed and the oil pump.

20.name: Magneto drive gear
20.note: Same tooth count as the crank gear, so each magneto turns once per crank turn and sparks twice, once for each of two cylinders.

21.name: Magneto
21.note: A self-contained generator and distributor: it makes its own spark from a spinning magnet, needing no battery. Two run independently.

22.name: Oil pump
22.note: Two meshing gears draw oil from the sump and push it through the filter and cooler to the bearings, cam and tappets.

23.name: Accessory housing
23.note: The engine's rear cover. It holds the drive gears and carries the magnetos, the oil pump and the other accessories on its back face.

24.name: Oil sump with induction riser
24.note: Holds the oil under the crank. The intake riser runs through it, so the warm oil heats the mixture and the mixture cools the oil.

25.name: Intake pipe
25.note: Carries the fuel–air mixture from the sump's riser up to each cylinder's inlet port.

26.name: Carburettor
26.note: Under the sump: air flows up through its venturi and draws fuel in by the pressure drop. Mixture is set from the cockpit.

27.name: Crankshaft oil seal
27.note: Seals the crank nose where it leaves the case, so oil stays in while the propeller flange turns outside.
